This part of the manual explains what is expected

Routine Service Standards

This section sets the daily expectations for the Companion Animal Travel Desk. Staff must give clear guidance before departure, keep records accurate, and keep the traveler informed at each step.

Work at the desk begins with a calm review of incoming requests and follow-up notes. The passenger coordinator explains the required travel steps in plain words, checks that documents are complete, and confirms any needed service details with the traveler. Staff should use steady language, avoid confusion, and keep the focus on practical next actions. When a passenger raises a concern, the first response is to listen, restate the issue, and offer the next available route for help. Routine questions are handled at the desk when possible, so the traveler does not need to repeat the same information.

The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions and should be informed when a case falls outside routine handling. Escalations move through a calm stepwise review, starting with the desk record, then the service check, and then any needed management decision. Staff must not promise an outcome before the review is complete. If a traveler has special concerns about a pet, the desk should note the issue clearly and keep all updates consistent across the service file. The tone should remain even, respectful, and brief, even when the conversation is tense.

Accuracy matters in every contact. Staff must file the latest information, confirm that the traveler has the correct guidance, and correct any mismatch as soon as it appears. If one part of the process changes, the desk should explain only what is confirmed and avoid adding guesswork. Coordination with the wider airport service team should stay focused on the traveler's immediate needs and on smooth handoff between roles.

If uncertainty remains after the desk review, contact the senior coordinator for direction and continue to support the traveler with clear, steady communication.
